# Pressed Petal: stallholder pack

Collection: botanical pictures.

## During public opening

- The public market runs from 10:00 until 16:00; keep the collection available during those hours.
- Use a single example of the frames to explain the collection rather than unpacking every spare.
- Keep the information card beside the cards even when the display is rearranged.
- Put any customer questions about the bookmarks on the page with their stock codes.
- Replace the panels price card if its writing becomes hard to read during the day.
- The spare miniatures are in the same box used for transport and need not all be displayed.
- Keep the prints sample with its descriptive card while showing it to a customer.
- When a group of tags sells out, remove that price card rather than leaving an empty group.
- Leave the last collages and postcards near their respective stock labels.

## Packing down

- Begin packing down after the public market closes at 16:00.
- Count the remaining frames against the opening list before putting them into their transport box.
- Return the cards label cards to the pouch used on the way to the market.
- Wrap the bookmarks separately from the display stands so the labels remain readable.
- Take all your unsold stock and packaging away; none is left for the venue to dispose of.
- Check beneath the table for the box that carried the panels and miniatures.
- Put the prints and tags sample cards in the notebook rather than with the wrapping scraps.
- Keep the return count of collages beside the sales record until you have checked it at home.
- Put the last postcards label on top of its bundle so it is easy to find on arrival home.

## Notes after the market

- Compare the remaining frames count with the entries in your sales notebook.
- Keep the customer questions about cards with the photographs of that collection.
- Write down whether another display stand would help show the bookmarks.
- Check whether the price cards for panels can be reused at the next market.
- Record any colour requests for miniatures without treating them as confirmed orders.
- Put the sample card for prints back in the display kit once you have finished the stock count.
- Keep the final packing list for tags with the matching box.
- Note which wrapping sizes were used for collages so the supplies can be replenished.
- File the postcards receipt copies with the rest of this market's paperwork.

## Stock for this visit

- Bring 11 frames from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 12 cards from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 13 bookmarks from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 14 panels from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 15 miniatures from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 16 prints from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 17 tags from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 18 collages from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 19 postcards from the Pressed Petal botanical pictures collection, with their matching stock labels.

## Packing the collection

- Put the frames in the first box, with a handwritten count on a card inside the lid.
- Wrap the cards separately so their labels are not hidden by the protective paper.
- Leave one example of the bookmarks near the top for setting up the front of the display.
- Bring your own table covering; the venue provides a bare table.
- Keep the price cards for panels with that group rather than in the general stationery bag.
- The miniatures go in the shallow box that can slide beneath the table during the market.
- Use the older packing sleeves for prints; their creases will be hidden underneath the display.
- Check that the small labels for tags have not stuck to the packing paper.
- Put the collages and postcards in separate bundles to simplify the opening stock count.

## Arrival and access

- The name on your stall envelope is Pressed Petal; keep the envelope with the collection until unpacking.
- Bring delivery vehicles to the Mill Lane gate for unloading; the High Street front steps are pedestrian access.
- Carry the lightweight frames box separately from the heavier display materials.
- Place the box of cards beside your own table while you unpack, within its marked space.
- Stallholder entry for setting up starts at 08:00; do not begin setting up before that time.
- Keep the label sheet for bookmarks to hand instead of leaving it in the vehicle.
- Put the empty transport bags beneath your own table once the panels are unpacked.
- Check the stall name against your envelope before laying out the stock.
- Do not leave a delivery vehicle blocking the unloading gate after the boxes are out.

## Building the display

- Place the frames on the left, with one label visible from the front of the table.
- Put the tallest cards behind the smaller pieces so they do not hide the price cards.
- Leave a clear patch beside the bookmarks for showing a customer the details of one piece.
- Keep every display and spare box inside the marked stall space so the aisle remains clear.
- Group the panels by finish, keeping the spare examples below their display group.
- Put the miniatures near the sample card that explains how that part of the collection was made.
- Lay out only a few prints at once and bring replacements from the stock box as they sell.
- The tags and collages use the two small stands from your own display kit.
- Keep the postcards label facing outward even when there is only one example left.

## Explaining the work

- The collection description calls these pieces botanical pictures, using the wording on your own labels.
- Show the back of a sample frames when a customer asks about its finish.
- Keep the sample for cards separate from the pieces counted as available stock.
- Explain that the bookmarks in this batch share a design, while small surface details vary.
- Use the photograph card to show the earlier stages of making the panels.
- Let the maker card answer questions about where the miniatures were made.
- The sketch beside the prints shows an alternative colour rather than another item for sale.
- Use the same collection names for tags on the display and on the receipt.
- Keep a sample label for collages and postcards in your notebook after the market.

## Prices and payments

- The price cards for frames belong beside that group, with the stock code facing you.
- Keep the replacement labels for cards in the stationery pouch rather than under the display.
- You supply and manage your own payment method; the free guest wireless network is available.
- Check the description on the receipt when a customer buys one of the bookmarks.
- Write the code for the panels in the sales notebook before wrapping the purchase.
- When two miniatures are sold together, record each stock code on its own entry.
- The sample prints stays marked as a sample so it is not included in the sold total.
- Keep a pencil beside the tags stock card for updating the remaining quantity.
- Check that descriptions for collages and postcards are readable on the receipt copy.

## Keeping track of stock

- Count the frames left in the box before putting replacements out on the table.
- Cross through the stock code when a displayed example of cards is sold.
- The spare labels for bookmarks use the same collection name as the display card.
- Keep the panels packing sleeves in their own box so their remaining count is easy to check.
- Make a note if a customer asks about another colour of miniatures.
- Put a mark beside the prints code when that design has only its display sample left.
- The stock card for tags stays with the notebook even if that group sells out.
- Check the count of collages before starting to pack them for the return journey.
- Keep the final count for postcards on the original stock card rather than on loose paper.

## Breaks and refreshments

- The cafe sells its own food and drinks separately from the goods on your stall.
- Leave the frames price card visible if you cover the stall while taking a break.
- Put the notebook beside the cards stock box so your companion can find it.
- Take used cafe mugs back to the cafe counter; do not leave them at the market exit.
- Keep cups off the display area beside the bookmarks and use your own small side tray instead.
- Leave the wrapping supplies for panels within reach of the person looking after the stall.
- Tell your companion which miniatures are samples before handing the stall over.
- Keep the prints and tags stock codes on the same page while the companion is helping.
- Use the notebook for questions about collages and postcards that need your answer later.

## Wrapping purchases

- Bring your own bags and wrapping; the venue does not supply packaging for purchases.
- Use a small piece of your packing paper between two frames bought together.
- Keep the labels with the cards when a customer wants them wrapped separately.
- Use the larger bag for the bookmarks instead of folding their information card.
- Check the receipt against the number of panels before sealing the bag.
- Put the maker card beside the miniatures so it can be read without unwrapping everything.
- The reused sleeves for prints are for transporting stock, not the customer display.
- Leave the labels readable when wrapping the tags and collages together.
- The smallest postcards fit in the shallow paper packets in your wrapping box.
